context.rule: The six basic strokes: 横 horizontal, 竖 vertical, 撇 left-falling, 捺 right-falling, 点 dot, 提 rising
context.en: The first stroke of 人 is the left-falling stroke.

why: 人 starts with the left-falling stroke 撇, then the right-falling stroke 捺.

not.捺: 捺 is the second stroke of 人, not the first.

context.rule: The six basic strokes: 横 horizontal, 竖 vertical, 撇 left-falling, 捺 right-falling, 点 dot, 提 rising
context.en: The first stroke of 十 is the horizontal stroke.

why: 十 is written with the horizontal stroke 横 first, then the vertical stroke 竖.

not.竖: 竖 comes second in 十.

context.rule: The six basic strokes: 横 horizontal, 竖 vertical, 撇 left-falling, 捺 right-falling, 点 dot, 提 rising
context.en: The first stroke of 六 is the dot.

why: 六 begins with a dot 点 at the top, then 横 below it.

not.横: 横 is the second stroke of 六.
not.撇: 撇 is the third stroke of 六.

context.rule: The six basic strokes: 横 horizontal, 竖 vertical, 撇 left-falling, 捺 right-falling, 点 dot, 提 rising
context.en: The third stroke of 汉 is the rising stroke.

why: 汉 has 氵 on the left: dot, dot, then the rising stroke 提 as the third stroke.

not.点: 点 is the first and second stroke of 汉.

context.rule: The six basic strokes: 横 horizontal, 竖 vertical, 撇 left-falling, 捺 right-falling, 点 dot, 提 rising
context.en: The last stroke of 大 is the right-falling stroke.

why: 大 ends with the right-falling stroke 捺: horizontal, left-falling, then 捺 last.

not.撇: 撇 is the second stroke of 大.
not.横: 横 is the first stroke of 大.

context.rule: Stroke order: horizontal before vertical, left-falling before right-falling, top to bottom, left to right, middle before sides, outside before inside
context.en: When writing 十, write the horizontal first, then the vertical.

why: The rule is horizontal before vertical, so after the 横 in 十 comes the vertical stroke 竖.

context.rule: Stroke order: horizontal before vertical, left-falling before right-falling, top to bottom, left to right, middle before sides, outside before inside
context.en: When writing 人, write the left-falling stroke first, then the right-falling one.

why: In 人 the left-falling stroke 撇 comes first, then the right-falling stroke 捺.

context.rule: Stroke order: horizontal before vertical, left-falling before right-falling, top to bottom, left to right, middle before sides, outside before inside
context.en: Write 三 from top to bottom.

why: Strokes go from top to bottom, and 三 is three horizontal lines stacked, so write it from top to 下.

not.左: 三 is stacked up and down, so left-to-right does not fit.
not.外: 外 is for characters with a frame, like 月.
not.右: 三 is not written from right to left.

context.rule: Stroke order: horizontal before vertical, left-falling before right-falling, top to bottom, left to right, middle before sides, outside before inside
context.en: When writing 小, write the middle first, then the two sides.

why: 小 follows the rule middle before sides: the middle stroke first, then 两边, the left and right dots.

not.上面: 小 has no top part; the middle stroke comes first.
not.下面: 小 is not written top then bottom.

context.rule: Stroke order: horizontal before vertical, left-falling before right-falling, top to bottom, left to right, middle before sides, outside before inside
context.en: When writing 月, write the outside first, then the inside.

why: 月 follows outside before inside: the frame first, then 里面, the two strokes inside.

not.左边: 月 starts with the frame, not a side part.
not.上面: 月 is not written top before bottom.
not.右边: The right side belongs to the frame, written first.

context.rule: Reading numbers: 十 ten, 百 hundred, 千 thousand, 万 ten thousand
context.en: 11 is read as 十一.

why: 11 is 十 (ten) plus 一 (one), so it is read 十一.

not.百: 十百 is not a number.
not.千: 十千 is not a number.

context.rule: Reading numbers: 十 ten, 百 hundred, 千 thousand, 万 ten thousand
context.en: 100 is read as 一百.

why: 100 is one hundred, 一百.

context.rule: Reading numbers: 十 ten, 百 hundred, 千 thousand, 万 ten thousand
context.en: 3000 is read as 三千.

why: 3000 is three thousand, 三千.

context.rule: Reading numbers: 十 ten, 百 hundred, 千 thousand, 万 ten thousand
context.en: 30000 is read as 三万.

why: 30000 is three ten-thousands, 三万.

context.rule: Reading numbers: 十 ten, 百 hundred, 千 thousand, 万 ten thousand
context.en: 36 is read as 三十六.

why: 36 is thirty and six: 三十 then 六, so 三十六.

not.十: 三十十 is not a number.

context.rule: 一 is yī alone; before a 4th tone it is yí; before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone it is yì
context.en: 一共 is read yígòng.

why: 一 changes to yí before a 4th tone, and 共 is gòng, 4th tone, so 一共 is yígòng.

not.yì: yì is used before 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone, but 共 is 4th tone.
not.yī: yī is the tone when 一 stands alone.
not.yǐ: yǐ is not a reading of 一.

context.rule: 一 is yī alone; before a 4th tone it is yí; before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone it is yì
context.en: 一起 is read yìqǐ.

why: 起 is 3rd tone (qǐ), and 一 before a 3rd tone is read yì.

not.yí: yí is used before a 4th tone; 起 is 3rd tone.
not.yī: yī is the tone when 一 stands alone.
not.yǐ: yǐ is not a reading of 一.

context.rule: 一 is yī alone; before a 4th tone it is yí; before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone it is yì
context.en: 一半 is read yíbàn.

why: 半 is bàn, 4th tone, and 一 before a 4th tone becomes yí.

not.yì: yì is for 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone; 半 is 4th tone.
not.yī: yī is the tone when 一 stands alone.
not.yǐ: yǐ is not a reading of 一.

context.rule: 一 is yī alone; before a 4th tone it is yí; before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone it is yì
context.en: 一点儿 is read yìdiǎnr.

why: 点 is diǎn, 3rd tone, and 一 before a 3rd tone is yì.

not.yí: yí is used before a 4th tone; 点 is 3rd tone.
not.yī: yī is the tone when 一 stands alone.
not.yǐ: yǐ is not a reading of 一.

context.rule: Derivative strokes are named by the basic strokes they pass through, in writing order
context.en: The second stroke of 山 is shù-zhé (vertical, turn right).

why: The second stroke of 山 goes down then turns right: 竖折.

not.竖: 竖 alone does not turn right.
not.横折: 横折 goes right first, then down.
not.撇折: 撇折 starts with a left-falling stroke.

context.rule: Derivative strokes are named by the basic strokes they pass through, in writing order
context.en: The second stroke of 心 is the lying hook.

why: The second stroke of 心 is the long curve with a hook, the lying hook 卧钩.

not.弯钩: 弯钩 is more upright than the long curve in 心.
not.点: 点 is the first, third and fourth stroke.

context.rule: Derivative strokes are named by the basic strokes they pass through, in writing order
context.en: The first stroke of 水 is the vertical hook.

why: 水 starts with a vertical line ending in a hook, 竖钩.

not.竖: 竖 has no hook, but this stroke does.
not.弯钩: 弯钩 is curved; this stroke is straight.
not.竖提: 竖提 turns up at the bottom without a hook.

context.rule: Derivative strokes are named by the basic strokes they pass through, in writing order
context.en: The second stroke of 九 is héng-zhé-wān-gōu.

why: 九 has 撇 first, then 横折弯钩, which goes across, down, curves and hooks.

not.横折钩: 横折钩 has no curve at the bottom.
not.竖弯钩: 竖弯钩 starts going down, not across.
not.撇折: 撇折 starts with a left-falling stroke.

context.rule: Derivative strokes are named by the basic strokes they pass through, in writing order
context.en: The second stroke of 子 is the curved hook.

why: 子 is written 横撇, then 弯钩, then 横. The middle stroke curves a little as it goes down, then hooks: 弯钩.

not.竖钩: 竖钩 is straight, as in 小; the stroke in 子 curves.
not.横折钩: 横折钩 turns at a corner; 子 has no such stroke.
not.卧钩: 卧钩 is the lying hook in 心.

context.rule: Derivative strokes are named by the basic strokes they pass through, in writing order
context.en: The second stroke of 儿 is the vertical-bend-hook.

why: 儿 has 撇 first, then 竖弯钩: down, curve right and hook up.

not.弯钩: 弯钩 is a curve without the straight part down first.
not.竖钩: 竖钩 has no bend to the right.
not.竖折: 竖折 ends in a corner, not a hook.

context.rule: Derivative strokes are named by the basic strokes they pass through, in writing order
context.en: The fifth stroke of 我 is the slanting hook.

why: 我 has a long slanting stroke with a hook as its fifth stroke: 斜钩.

not.竖钩: 竖钩 is the third stroke of 我, a straight hook.
not.横折钩: 横折钩 turns at a corner.
not.弯钩: 弯钩 is a gentle curve; 我 has a slanting one.

context.rule: Idioms with numbers
context.en: His room is a complete mess.

why: 乱七八糟 means very messy; the idiom uses 七八 (seven, eight) with 乱 and 糟.

not.一: 一 is used in other idioms, such as 一心一意.
not.三: 三 does not fit this idiom.
not.十: 十 does not fit this idiom.

context.rule: Idioms with numbers
context.en: The flowers in the garden are colourful.

why: 五颜六色 is a set phrase meaning colourful: 五 + 颜 + 六 + 色.

not.样: 样 is not in this idiom.
not.半: 半 is not in this idiom.
not.些: 些 is not in this idiom.

context.rule: Idioms with numbers
context.en: Studying needs your whole heart.

why: 一心一意 is the idiom for doing something with full attention.

not.二: 二 gives 三心二意, a different idiom.
not.三: 三 does not fit this idiom.
not.七: 七 does not fit this idiom.

q: 做作业要专心，不要三心___意。

context.rule: Idioms with numbers
context.en: Concentrate on your homework; don't be half-hearted.

why: 三心二意 means being half-hearted, which fits the warning about not being focused.

not.一: 一心一意 means focused, the opposite.
not.四: 四 does not form this idiom.
not.五: 五 does not form this idiom.

context.rule: Idioms with numbers
context.en: Your guess is pretty close.

why: 八九不离十 is a fixed phrase meaning very close to right.

not.百: 百 does not form this phrase.
not.千: 千 does not form this phrase.
not.万: 万 does not form this phrase.

context.rule: Pictographs began as simple drawings of the thing itself; over time the lines became strokes
context.en: The character that looks like the sun is 日.

why: 日 comes from a picture of the sun, so it means sun.

not.火: 火 is fire, drawn with flames.
not.水: 水 is water, drawn with flowing lines.

q: 看上去像弯弯的月亮的字是“___”。

context.rule: Pictographs began as simple drawings of the thing itself; over time the lines became strokes
context.en: The character that looks like a crescent moon is 月.

why: 月 comes from a crescent moon.

q: 像一个侧面站着的人的字是“___”。

context.rule: Pictographs began as simple drawings of the thing itself; over time the lines became strokes
context.en: The character that looks like a person standing in profile is 人.

why: 人 is a person seen from the side, with two legs.

context.rule: Pictographs began as simple drawings of the thing itself; over time the lines became strokes
context.en: The character that looks like a fish is 鱼.

why: 鱼 means fish, and its shape comes from a fish.

context.rule: Pictographs began as simple drawings of the thing itself; over time the lines became strokes
context.en: Water falling from the sky is written 雨.

why: 雨 means rain; the dots inside it are raindrops falling from the sky.

not.水: 水 is water in general, not falling from the sky.

context.rule: Words made from the lesson's characters
context.en: He takes the train to Beijing.

why: 坐火车 means to take the train, and 坐 goes with vehicles.

not.火腿: 火腿 is ham, not a vehicle.

context.rule: Words made from the lesson's characters
context.en: It's raining; I need to take an umbrella.

why: 下雨了 means it is raining, so you bring an umbrella 雨伞.

context.rule: Words made from the lesson's characters
context.en: I drink milk for breakfast.

why: 喝 means to drink, and 牛奶 is a drink.

not.火腿: 火腿 is ham; you eat it, not drink it.
not.苹果: 苹果 is an apple; you eat it.

context.rule: Words made from the lesson's characters
context.en: Apples and mangoes are both fruit.

why: 苹果 and 芒果 are both kinds of 水果, fruit.

q: 我的儿子和女儿都是我的___。

context.rule: Words made from the lesson's characters
context.en: My son and my daughter are both my children.

why: Sons and daughters are your 孩子, children.

context.rule: Family, royal and 开 words
context.en: The son of the king and queen is the prince.

why: The son of a king and queen is a prince, 王子.

context.rule: Family, royal and 开 words
context.en: Dad drives to work every day.

why: 开车 means to drive a car, and it fits going to work every day.

not.火车: 火车 is a train, not an action.

context.rule: Family, royal and 开 words
context.en: It's my birthday today and I am very happy.

why: It is the speaker's birthday, so they feel 开心, happy.

q: 我最喜欢吃___，它是一种鱼。

context.rule: Family, royal and 开 words
context.en: I like salmon best; it's a kind of fish.

why: 三文鱼 is salmon, and the sentence says it is a fish.

not.开心果: 开心果 is pistachio, a nut.

q: 在“木”的下边加一横，就是“___”。

context.rule: Indicative characters: a mark added to a picture shows an idea that is hard to draw
context.en: Adding a stroke below 木 gives 本, the root of a tree.

why: Adding a stroke at the bottom of 木 marks the root: 本.

not.末: 末 has the long stroke on top.
not.天: 天 is built from 大, not 木.
not.太: 太 is built from 大, not 木.

q: 在“木”的上边加一长横，就是“___”。

context.rule: Indicative characters: a mark added to a picture shows an idea that is hard to draw
context.en: Adding a long stroke above 木 gives 末, the treetop.

why: A long stroke on top of 木 marks the treetop: 末.

not.本: 本 has the stroke at the bottom.
not.中: 中 is not made from 木.
not.片: 片 is not made from 木.

q: 在“大”的下边加一点，就是“___”。

context.rule: Indicative characters: a mark added to a picture shows an idea that is hard to draw
context.en: Adding a dot under 大 gives 太.

why: Adding a dot under 大 makes 太.

not.天: 天 has a stroke on top of 大.
not.本: 本 is made from 木.
not.末: 末 is made from 木.

q: 在“大”的上边加一横，就是“___”。

context.rule: Indicative characters: a mark added to a picture shows an idea that is hard to draw
context.en: Adding a stroke above 大 gives 天, the sky above a person's head.

why: A long stroke on top of 大 makes 天.

not.太: 太 has a dot under 大.
not.中: 中 is not made from 大.
not.片: 片 is not made from 大.

q: 我___去了商店，今天不去了。

context.rule: 昨天 yesterday, 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 每天 every day
context.en: I went to the shop yesterday; I am not going today.

why: 昨天 means yesterday; the sentence says I went (去了) and am not going today.

not.明天: 明天 is tomorrow; 去了 is past.

q: 我___喝一杯牛奶，一天一杯。

context.rule: 昨天 yesterday, 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 每天 every day
context.en: I drink a glass of milk every day, one a day.

why: 每天 means every day, which matches 一天一杯.

context.rule: 昨天 yesterday, 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 每天 every day
context.en: Tomorrow we are going to Beijing.

why: 要去北京 is a plan, so it goes with 明天, tomorrow.

not.昨天: 昨天 is yesterday; 要去 is future.
not.下班: 下班 is when work ends; a trip fits a day like 明天.
not.上课: 上课 means class starts; a trip fits a day like 明天.

q: 今天的___很好，不冷也不热。

context.rule: 昨天 yesterday, 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 每天 every day
context.en: Today's weather is nice, neither cold nor hot.

why: 不冷也不热 describes the weather, so 天气.

not.昨天: 昨天 is yesterday, not a thing that is nice.
not.中文: 中文 is the Chinese language.

context.rule: 上课 starts class, 下课 ends it; 上班 starts work, 下班 ends it
context.en: Class starts at eight and we begin to study.

why: 上课 means class starts, which matches 开始学习.

not.下班: 下班 means to leave work.

context.rule: 上课 starts class, 下课 ends it; 上班 starts work, 下班 ends it
context.en: Class ends at twelve and we go to eat.

why: 下课 means class ends, then we go to eat.

not.上班: 上班 means to start work.
not.上网: 上网 means to go online.

context.rule: 上课 starts class, 下课 ends it; 上班 starts work, 下班 ends it
context.en: Dad finishes work at five, then goes home.

why: Dad finishes work at five and goes home: 下班.

not.上班: 上班 means to start work.

q: 我___在家看电影，下午去商店。

context.rule: 上课 starts class, 下课 ends it; 上班 starts work, 下班 ends it
context.en: In the morning I watch a film at home; in the afternoon I go to the shop.

why: The sentence contrasts with 下午 (afternoon), so the first part is 上午, morning.

not.下午: 下午 is used in the second part.
not.期末: 期末 is the end of term.

q: 一个人靠着一棵树，就是“___”。

context.rule: Associative characters: the meanings of the parts together give the meaning of the whole
context.en: A person leaning on a tree makes 休, to rest.

why: A person 亻 leaning on a tree 木 makes 休, to rest.

not.看: 看 is a hand above an eye.

q: 日和月在一起，就是“___”，意思是很亮。

context.rule: Associative characters: the meanings of the parts together give the meaning of the whole
context.en: Sun and moon together make 明, bright.

why: 日 (sun) and 月 (moon) together make 明, bright.

not.比: 比 is two people side by side.

q: 女和子在一起，就是“___”，意思是不错。

context.rule: Associative characters: the meanings of the parts together give the meaning of the whole
context.en: Woman and child together make 好, good.

why: 女 (woman) and 子 (child) together make 好.

not.美: 美 is not made of 女 and 子.
not.家: 家 is a roof over a pig.
not.坐: 坐 is two people on the ground.

context.rule: Associative characters: the meanings of the parts together give the meaning of the whole
context.en: A hand above the eye makes 看, to look.

why: A hand over the eye makes 看, to look.

not.有: 有 is not about the eye.
not.友: 友 is not about the eye.

q: 两只脚一前一后，就是“___”，意思是走路。

context.rule: Associative characters: the meanings of the parts together give the meaning of the whole
context.en: Two feet, one after the other, make 步, a step.

why: Two feet one after the other show walking, 步.

q: 写“安”的时候，先写上面的“宀”，再写下面的“___”。

context.rule: Stroke order: top before bottom, left before right, a roof comes first
context.en: When writing 安, write the roof 宀 first, then the 女 below it.

why: 安 has the roof 宀 on top and 女 below.

not.子: 子 is not under the roof in 安.
not.口: 口 is not in 安.
not.木: 木 is not in 安.

q: 写“明”的时候，先写左边的“___”，再写右边的“月”。

context.rule: Stroke order: top before bottom, left before right, a roof comes first
context.en: When writing 明, write the left part 日 first, then 月.

why: 明 is written left to right: 日 on the left first, then 月.

not.月: 月 is the right part, written second.
not.目: 目 has one more line; the left of 明 is 日.
not.田: 田 is not in 明.

q: 写“美”的时候，先写上面的“羊”，再写下面的“___”。

context.rule: Stroke order: top before bottom, left before right, a roof comes first
context.en: When writing 美, write 羊 above first, then 大 below.

why: 美 is 羊 on top and 大 below, written top to bottom.

not.天: The bottom of 美 is 大, not 天.
not.小: 小 is not in 美.
not.火: 火 is not in 美.

q: 写“笔”的时候，先写上面的“竹”，再写下面的“___”。

context.rule: Stroke order: top before bottom, left before right, a roof comes first
context.en: When writing 笔, write the bamboo top first, then 毛 below.

why: 笔 has 竹 on top and 毛 below.

not.手: 手 is not in 笔.
not.木: 木 is not in 笔.
not.水: 水 is not in 笔.

q: 这个菜很___，我还想再吃一碗。

context.rule: 好 + verb means nice to do it: 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good to look at), 好玩儿 (fun)
context.en: This dish is tasty, I want another bowl.

why: The speaker wants another bowl, so the dish tastes good: 好吃.

not.好看: 好看 is about looks; wanting more means it tastes good.
not.好玩儿: 好玩儿 is about fun activities.

context.rule: 好 + verb means nice to do it: 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good to look at), 好玩儿 (fun)
context.en: Her new clothes look nice.

why: Clothes are nice to look at, so 好看.

not.好玩儿: 好玩儿 is for fun activities.

q: 这个游戏很___，我们玩儿了一天。

context.rule: 好 + verb means nice to do it: 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good to look at), 好玩儿 (fun)
context.en: This game is fun; we played it all day.

why: A game you play all day is 好玩儿, fun.

context.rule: 好 + verb means nice to do it: 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good to look at), 好玩儿 (fun)
context.en: You have an exam tomorrow, good luck!

why: Before an exam we wish good luck: 祝你好运.

context.rule: Pictophonetic characters: one part shows the meaning, one part hints at the sound
context.en: In 妈, 女 shows the meaning and 马 hints at the sound.

why: 妈 has 女 for meaning and 马 for sound (mǎ and mā are close).

not.母: 母 means mother but is not a part of 妈.
not.吗: 吗 is a different character, not a part of 妈.
not.好: 好 is not a part of 妈.

context.rule: Pictophonetic characters: one part shows the meaning, one part hints at the sound
context.en: In 海, 氵 shows the meaning and 每 hints at the sound.

why: 海 is 氵 plus 每. 每 is the sound part, though today měi and hǎi sound less alike.

not.母: 母 is not in 海.
not.毒: 毒 is not in 海.
not.木: 木 is not in 海.

context.rule: Pictophonetic characters: one part shows the meaning, one part hints at the sound
context.en: In 汁, 氵 shows the meaning and 十 hints at the sound.

why: 汁 is 氵 plus 十; 十 (shí) sounds close to 汁 (zhī).

not.千: 千 is not in 汁.
not.干: 干 is not in 汁.
not.土: 土 is not in 汁.

context.rule: Pictophonetic characters: one part shows the meaning, one part hints at the sound
context.en: In 问, 口 shows the meaning and 门 hints at the sound.

why: 问 is 口 inside 门; 门 (mén) gives the sound, close to wèn.

not.日: 日 is not in 问.
not.马: 马 is not in 问.
not.女: 女 is not in 问.

context.rule: Common meaning parts: 亻 person, 口 mouth, 女 woman, 氵 water, 日 sun or time
context.en: Characters with 氵 are mostly related to water.

why: 氵 is the water radical, so these characters are about 水.

not.人: Characters about people use 亻, not 氵.

context.rule: Common meaning parts: 亻 person, 口 mouth, 女 woman, 氵 water, 日 sun or time
context.en: Characters with 口 are mostly related to the mouth.

why: 口 is a mouth, so these characters are about the mouth 嘴.

q: 有“日”的字多和太阳、___有关。

context.rule: Common meaning parts: 亻 person, 口 mouth, 女 woman, 氵 water, 日 sun or time
context.en: Characters with 日 are mostly related to the sun and time.

why: 日 is the sun and also days, so it relates to time 时间.

context.rule: Common meaning parts: 亻 person, 口 mouth, 女 woman, 氵 water, 日 sun or time
context.en: 喝, 唱 and 问 all contain 口.

why: 喝, 唱 and 问 all contain 口 (mouth).

not.日: 日 is not in these characters.
not.氵: 氵 is not in these characters.
not.女: 女 is not in these characters.

context.rule: Which meaning part? Group the characters you know
context.en: 奶, 婚 and 妈 all have 女 as their meaning part.

why: 奶, 婚 and 妈 are all connected to women, with 女.

not.子: 子 is not in 奶.
not.口: 口 is not in 奶.
not.日: 日 is not in 奶.

context.rule: Which meaning part? Group the characters you know
context.en: 洗, 游 and 汁 all have 氵 as their meaning part.

why: 洗, 游 and 汁 all have the water radical 氵.

not.口: 口 is not in 洗.
not.日: 日 is not in 洗.

context.rule: Which meaning part? Group the characters you know
context.en: 晚, 时 and 星 all have 日 as their meaning part.

why: 晚, 时 and 星 all have 日 on the left or top.

not.月: 月 is not in 晚.
not.目: 目 is not in 晚.
not.田: 田 is not in 晚.

context.rule: Which meaning part? Group the characters you know
context.en: 作, 信 and 休 all have 亻 as their meaning part.

why: 作, 信 and 休 all have the person radical 亻 on the left.

not.口: 口 is not in 作.
not.女: 女 is not in 作.

context.rule: A pictophonetic character has a sound part (声符) that hints at how it is read
context.en: 青 is the sound part in 清, 请, 情 and 晴.

why: 清, 请, 情 and 晴 all contain 青 (qīng), so they all sound like qing.

not.氵: 氵 is the meaning part of 清 only.
not.讠: 讠 is the meaning part of 请 only.
not.日: 日 is the meaning part of 晴 only.

context.rule: A pictophonetic character has a sound part (声符) that hints at how it is read
context.en: 包 is the sound part in 饱, 抱, 跑 and 泡.

why: 饱, 抱, 跑 and 泡 all contain 包 (bāo), giving a similar sound.

not.饣: 饣 is the meaning part of 饱.
not.扌: 扌 is the meaning part of 抱.
not.足: 足 is the meaning part of 跑.

context.rule: A pictophonetic character has a sound part (声符) that hints at how it is read
context.en: 马 is the sound part in 妈, 吗, 码 and 骂.

why: 妈, 吗, 码 and 骂 all contain 马 (mǎ) for the sound.

not.女: 女 is the meaning part of 妈 only.
not.口: 口 is the meaning part of 吗 only.
not.石: 石 is the meaning part of 码 only.

context.rule: A pictophonetic character has a sound part (声符) that hints at how it is read
context.en: The sound part of 排 is 非, and the sounds are close.

why: 排 is 扌 (hand) plus 非. 非 is the sound part, though fēi and pái sound less alike today.

not.手: 手 is the full form of 扌, the meaning part.
not.白: 白 is not in 排.
not.牛: 牛 is not in 排.

q: 说、讨、记、试都有意符___，和说话有关。

context.rule: A meaning part (意符) hints at the meaning
context.en: 说, 讨, 记 and 试 all have 讠, which is about speaking.

why: 说, 讨, 记 and 试 all have 讠, the speech radical.

not.月: 月 is the moon or flesh radical.

q: 树、桃、梯、校都有意符___，和树木有关。

context.rule: A meaning part (意符) hints at the meaning
context.en: 树, 桃, 梯 and 校 all have 木, which is about trees.

why: 树, 桃, 梯 and 校 all have 木, which is about trees and wood.

q: 眼、睛、睡、看都有意符___，和眼睛有关。

context.rule: A meaning part (意符) hints at the meaning
context.en: 眼, 睛, 睡 and 看 all have 目, which is about the eyes.

why: 眼, 睛, 睡 and 看 all have 目, which is the eye.

q: 雪、雾、零、霉都有意符___，和天气有关。

context.rule: A meaning part (意符) hints at the meaning
context.en: 雪, 雾, 零 and 霉 all have 雨, which is about weather.

why: 雪, 雾, 零 and 霉 all have 雨 on top; they relate to weather.

q: “期”的右边是___，和月亮、时间有关。

context.rule: A meaning part (意符) hints at the meaning
context.en: The right side of 期 is 月, linked to the moon and time.

why: 期 has 其 on the left and 月 on the right; 月 links to time.

q: “忘”的意符是心，声符是___，也有“逃走”的意思。

context.rule: Sometimes the sound part also gives the meaning
context.en: In 忘 the meaning part is 心 and the sound part is 亡, which also means "to escape".

why: 忘 is 亡 above 心; 亡 means to flee and gives the sound wáng.

not.女: 女 is not in 忘.
not.取: 取 is not in 忘.
not.青: 青 is not in 忘.

q: “娶”的意符是女，声符是___，也有“取得”的意思。

context.rule: Sometimes the sound part also gives the meaning
context.en: In 娶 the meaning part is 女 and the sound part is 取, which also means "to get".

why: 娶 is 取 above 女; 取 means to take, and gives the sound qǔ.

not.亡: 亡 is the sound part of 忘.
not.心: 心 is the meaning part of 忘.
not.包: 包 is the sound part of 饱.

q: 形声字的声符不一定和整个字读音___一样。

context.rule: Sometimes the sound part also gives the meaning
context.en: The sound part of a pictophonetic character is not always exactly the same in reading as the whole character.

why: 完全一样 means exactly the same. The sound part often only sounds close, like 每 měi in 海 hǎi.

not.一定: 一定 clashes with 不一定 earlier in the sentence.
not.总是: 总是 means always; the English says exactly, which is 完全.
not.都: 都 needs several things; here one part is compared with one character.

context.rule: Look-alike characters: similar shapes, different meanings
context.en: You're tired; rest at home for a while.

why: 休息 means to rest; 休 is a person leaning on a tree.

context.rule: Look-alike characters: similar shapes, different meanings
context.en: I am in good health.

why: 身体 means body or health; 身 goes before 体.

not.休: 休 is for 休息, not 体.

context.rule: Look-alike characters: similar shapes, different meanings
context.en: I live next to the school.

why: 住在 means to live at; 住 has 亻 and 主.

context.rule: Look-alike characters: similar shapes, different meanings
context.en: Please go straight ahead; the shop is there.

why: 往前走 means to go forward; 往 is a direction word.

context.rule: Look-alike characters: similar shapes, different meanings
context.en: This is my classmate, called Xiao Wang.

why: 同学 means classmate.

not.字: 同字 is not a word.
not.高: 同高 is not a word.
not.商: 同商 is not a word.

context.rule: Homophones: different characters, the same sound
context.en: My dad works at a company.

why: 工作 means to work. 工 and 公 both sound gōng, but only 工 makes 工作.

not.公: 公 makes 公司 (company), not 公作.

context.rule: Homophones: different characters, the same sound
context.en: She is a doctor and works at a hospital.

why: 医生 means doctor, and she works in a hospital 医院.

not.衣: 衣 sounds like 医 but means clothes.
not.工: 工 makes 工作, not 工生.
not.公: 公 makes 公司, not 公生.

context.rule: Homophones: different characters, the same sound
context.en: This piece of clothing is blue.

why: 衣服 means clothes, and the sentence mentions its colour.

context.rule: Homophones: different characters, the same sound
context.en: He plays basketball very well.

why: 篮球 means basketball; 篮 has the bamboo top for baskets.

not.堂: 堂 is in 教堂 and 食堂.

context.rule: Homophones: different characters, the same sound
context.en: The sky is blue.

why: 蓝色 means the colour blue, and 蓝 has the grass top.

q: 这条路很___，走了半个小时。

context.rule: Polyphonic characters: one character, more than one reading
context.en: This road is long; the walk took half an hour.

why: 很长 describes a long road; here 长 is cháng and means long.

not.常: 常 means often; it cannot describe a road.
not.场: 场 is a measure word for games and shows, not an adjective.

context.rule: Polyphonic characters: one character, more than one reading
context.en: The kitten has grown up. (read zhǎng)

why: 长大 means grow up; 长 is read zhǎng here.

not.常: 常大 is not a word.
not.堂: 堂大 is not a word.
not.场: 场大 is not a word.

context.rule: Polyphonic characters: one character, more than one reading
context.en: I love listening to music. (read yuè)

why: 音乐 means music; here 乐 is read yuè.

context.rule: Polyphonic characters: one character, more than one reading
context.en: My hobby is swimming. (read hào)

why: 爱好 means hobby; here 好 is read hào.

not.号: 号 is read hào but 爱号 is not a word.
not.如: 如 does not fit after 爱.
not.她: 她 does not fit after 爱.

context.rule: Polyphonic characters: one character, more than one reading
context.en: This cup is cheap. (read pián)

why: 便宜 means cheap, read piányi; 便 is read pián here.

not.使: 使 does not form 使宜.
not.更: 更 does not form 更宜.
not.但: 但 does not form 但宜.

q: “苹”不能单用，要和“果”一起组成词“___”。

context.rule: Most characters can stand alone as a word (火, 牛, 好), but some must join another character to make a word (苹 + 果).
context.en: 苹 cannot be used alone; together with 果 it makes the word 苹果 (apple).

why: 苹 is not used alone; it mainly appears in 苹果, apple.

not.果苹: 果苹 is the wrong order.
not.苹子: 苹子 is not a word.
not.苹菜: 苹菜 is not a word.

q: “好”是一个字，也可以单独当一个___用。

context.rule: Most characters can stand alone as a word (火, 牛, 好), but some must join another character to make a word (苹 + 果).
context.en: 好 is one character and can also be used alone as a word.

why: 好 can stand alone as a word, for example 很好.

not.笔画: 笔画 are strokes, not a word type.

q: “花儿”是两个汉字，但是只有一个___。

context.rule: Most characters can stand alone as a word (火, 牛, 好), but some must join another character to make a word (苹 + 果).
context.en: 花儿 is two characters but only one syllable (huār).

why: 花儿 has two characters but one syllable, huār.

not.笔画: 笔画 are strokes; 花儿 has many.

context.rule: Many one-syllable words became two-syllable words. “子” in 杯子, 桌子 is a suffix with no real meaning.
context.en: Long ago people used 目 for the eye; now we say 眼睛.

why: Long ago 目 meant eye; today people say 眼睛.

q: “杯子”里的“子”没有实际意思，是___。

context.rule: Many one-syllable words became two-syllable words. “子” in 杯子, 桌子 is a suffix with no real meaning.
context.en: The 子 in 杯子 has no real meaning; it is a suffix.

why: 子 in 杯子 has no meaning of its own; it is a noun suffix 词缀.

not.动词: 子 is not a verb here.
not.名字: 子 is not a name here.

context.rule: Many one-syllable words became two-syllable words. “子” in 杯子, 桌子 is a suffix with no real meaning.
context.en: There is a big table in my home.

why: 桌子 means table; 子 is the suffix after 桌.

not.员: 桌员 is not a word.
not.语: 桌语 is not a word.
not.现: 桌现 is not a word.

q: 电话、电脑、电子邮件都有“___”。

context.rule: One character can build many words: the shared character gives the shared meaning.
context.en: 电话, 电脑 and 电子邮件 all contain 电 (electricity).

why: 电话, 电脑 and 电子邮件 all contain 电.

not.菜: 菜 is not in these words.
not.手: 手 is not in 电话.
not.球: 球 is not in 电话.

q: 生菜、菜单、白菜都和“___”有关。

context.rule: One character can build many words: the shared character gives the shared meaning.
context.en: 生菜, 菜单 and 白菜 are all related to 菜 (vegetables, dishes).

why: 生菜, 菜单 and 白菜 all have 菜.

not.色: 色 is not in these words.
not.面: 面 is not in these words.
not.语: 语 is not in these words.

context.rule: One character can build many words: the shared character gives the shared meaning.
context.en: 足球, 网球 and 羽毛球 are all kinds of ball (球).

why: 足球, 网球 and 羽毛球 all have 球.

not.鞋: 鞋 is not in these words.
not.肉: 肉 is not in these words.
not.员: 员 is not in these words.

q: 服务员、售货员、演员都有“___”。

context.rule: One character can build many words: the shared character gives the shared meaning.
context.en: 服务员, 售货员 and 演员 all contain 员, a person doing a job.

why: 服务员, 售货员 and 演员 all end with 员, a worker or member.

not.现: 现 is not in these words.
not.语: 语 is not in these words.
not.肉: 肉 is not in these words.

context.rule: Counting strokes: write each stroke in order, then add them up.
context.en: 电 has 5 strokes in total.

why: 电 has 5 strokes: 竖, 横折, 横, 横, 竖弯钩.

context.rule: Counting strokes: write each stroke in order, then add them up.
context.en: 肉 has 6 strokes in total.

why: 肉 has 6 strokes.

context.rule: Counting strokes: write each stroke in order, then add them up.
context.en: 现 has 8 strokes in total.

why: 现 is 王 (4 strokes) plus 见 (4 strokes), so 8.

context.rule: Join one component from each side to make a new character.
context.en: 亻 + 门 makes 们 (plural marker).

why: 亻 (person) plus 门 makes 们, the plural marker.

not.间: 间 is 门 plus 日.
not.问: 问 is 门 plus 口.
not.同: 同 is not 亻 plus 门.

context.rule: Join one component from each side to make a new character.
context.en: 女 + 也 makes 她 (she).

why: 女 (woman) plus 也 makes 她, she.

not.他: 他 is 亻 plus 也.
not.地: 地 is 土 plus 也.
not.池: 池 is 氵 plus 也.

context.rule: Join one component from each side to make a new character.
context.en: 氵 + 每 makes 海 (sea).

why: 氵 (water) plus 每 makes 海, sea.

not.梅: 梅 is 木 plus 每.
not.悔: 悔 is 忄 plus 每.
not.每: 每 is only one part; the answer adds 氵 to it.

context.rule: Join one component from each side to make a new character.
context.en: 日 + 乍 makes 昨 (as in yesterday).

why: 日 (sun) plus 乍 makes 昨, as in 昨天.

not.作: 作 is 亻 plus 乍.
not.怎: 怎 is 乍 plus 心.
not.炸: 炸 is 火 plus 乍.

context.rule: In many characters one part shows the meaning and the other part shows the sound.
context.en: In 吗 the 马 on the right shows the sound.

why: In 吗 the 口 is the meaning part and 马 gives the sound, mǎ.

not.意思: The meaning part is 口, not 马.
not.笔画: A part does not show stroke count.
not.颜色: Nothing in 吗 shows a colour.

q: 说、语、话的左边都是“___”，和说话有关。

context.rule: In many characters one part shows the meaning and the other part shows the sound.
context.en: 说, 语 and 话 all have 讠 on the left, related to speech.

why: 说, 语 and 话 all have 讠 on the left, the speech radical.

q: 海、泳、池的左边都是“___”，和水有关。

context.rule: In many characters one part shows the meaning and the other part shows the sound.
context.en: 海, 泳 and 池 all have 氵 on the left, related to water.

why: 海, 泳 and 池 all have 氵, the water radical.

context.rule: Pick the word that fits the sentence.
context.en: The teacher told us there is no class tomorrow.

why: 告诉 means to tell, and the teacher tells us something.

context.rule: Pick the word that fits the sentence.
context.en: There is a football match tonight.

why: 足球比赛 means a football match; 一场 goes with 比赛.

q: 这件衣服很___，只要二十块。

context.rule: Pick the word that fits the sentence.
context.en: This piece of clothing is very cheap, only twenty yuan.

why: 便宜 means cheap, which fits the price 二十块.
